chunks.text: This HR Policy Handbook applies to all full-time, part-time, and contract employees of the company. It establishes the standards of conduct, benefits, and responsibilities that govern the employment relationship. Employees are expected to read and acknowledge this handbook within their first week of joining.

Working Hours: Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, with a one-hour lunch break. Flexible working arrangements may be approved by an employee's reporting manager on a case-by-case basis, provided core collaboration hours of 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM are maintained.

Performance Reviews: Formal performance appraisals are conducted twice a year, in April and October. Reviews assess goal completion, competency development, and behavioral alignment with company values. Ratings directly influence annual merit increases and promotion eligibility.

Code of Conduct & Grievance Redressal: Employees who experience or witness workplace harassment, discrimination, or policy violations should report the issue to HR via the confidential grievance portal. All complaints are investigated within 10 business days and outcomes are communicated in writing to the complainant.

Termination & Notice Period: Employees are required to serve a notice period of 60 days for resignation, or as specified in their offer letter. The company reserves the right to provide pay-in-lieu of notice. Full and final settlement is processed within 45 days of the last working day.

Leave Entitlement: Employees are entitled to 18 days of Paid Time Off (PTO), 12 days of Sick Leave, and 10 public holidays per calendar year. Leave accrues monthly at a rate of 1.5 days of PTO. Unused PTO up to 10 days may be carried forward to the next calendar year.

Applying for Leave: All leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least 3 working days in advance, except in cases of medical emergency. Leave requests are auto-escalated to the reporting manager for approval and must be approved before the leave start date.

Maternity & Paternity Leave: Female employees are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave in accordance with statutory requirements. Paternity leave of 2 weeks is granted to male employees within 3 months of the child's birth or adoption.

Sick Leave & Medical Certification: Sick leave exceeding 2 consecutive days requires a medical certificate submitted to HR within 3 working days of return. Unauthorized absence beyond 3 consecutive days without notice may be treated as job abandonment.

Leave Without Pay (LWP): Employees who exhaust their leave balance may request Leave Without Pay, subject to manager and HR approval. LWP exceeding 30 days in a calendar year requires Director-level sign-off and may affect increment eligibility.

Purpose & Scope: This IT Security Policy defines the minimum security standards for all employees, contractors, and third parties accessing company systems, networks, and data. Non-compliance may result in disciplinary action, including termination of access or employment.

Password & Authentication: All company accounts must use passwords with a minimum of 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is mandatory for VPN, email, and all cloud administration consoles. Passwords must be rotated every 90 days.

Data Classification & Handling: Company data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted. Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+), and must never be stored on personal devices or unsanctioned cloud storage services.

Acceptable Use: Company-issued laptops and accounts are provided for business use. Installation of unauthorized software, disabling of endpoint antivirus/EDR agents, or connecting to untrusted public Wi-Fi without VPN is strictly prohibited.

Incident Reporting: Any suspected phishing email, malware infection, lost device, or data breach must be reported to the Security Operations Center (SOC) within 1 hour of discovery via security@company.com or the internal incident hotline. Delayed reporting may compound breach impact.

Our Code of Conduct sets out the ethical and professional standards expected of every employee. It covers integrity, respect, confidentiality, and compliance with applicable laws in every jurisdiction where the company operates.

Anti-Harassment & Non-Discrimination: The company maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward harassment, bullying, or discrimination based on race, gender, religion, disability, age, or sexual orientation. All employees complete mandatory anti-harassment training annually.

Conflict of Interest: Employees must disclose any personal, financial, or familial relationships that could reasonably be seen to influence business decisions, including vendor selection, hiring, or procurement. Disclosures are reviewed by the Ethics Committee.

Confidentiality & Intellectual Property: All work product, source code, designs, and client data created during employment are the exclusive property of the company. Employees must not disclose confidential information during or after employment without written authorization.
Gifts & Anti-Bribery: Employees may not accept gifts, hospitality, or kickbacks exceeding $75 in value from vendors, clients, or partners without prior disclosure to their manager and Compliance.

This policy governs the reimbursement of business-related travel and expenses. All expenses must be pre-approved by the reporting manager where the estimated cost exceeds $500, and submitted through the Expense Management System within 15 days of being incurred.

Travel Booking: Domestic flights must be booked in economy class; business class is permitted only for flights exceeding 6 hours with Director-level approval. Hotel bookings should not exceed the per-city rate cap published on the internal Travel Portal.
Meals & Per Diem: Employees on domestic business travel are entitled to a per diem of $60/day for meals and incidentals. Itemized receipts are required for any single expense exceeding $25.

Client Entertainment: Client meals and entertainment expenses require the client name, business purpose, and attendee list to be logged. Alcohol expenses are reimbursable up to a $100 cap per event and must comply with local regulations.

Non-Reimbursable Items: Personal entertainment, traffic or parking fines, spa services, and expenses lacking valid receipts will not be reimbursed. Fraudulent expense claims are grounds for immediate termination.

Welcome to the company! This Onboarding Guide walks new hires through their first 30 days, covering account provisioning, mandatory training, team introductions, and key policies every employee should know.

Day 1 Checklist: Collect your company laptop and badge from IT Helpdesk, complete identity verification, set up your corporate email and MFA, and join the '#new-joiners' Slack channel for onboarding announcements.

Mandatory Training: All new hires must complete Information Security Awareness, Anti-Harassment, and Code of Conduct training modules within the first 2 weeks via the Learning Management System (LMS). Completion is tracked by HR and required before probation review.

Probation Period: New employees undergo a 90-day probation period during which performance and cultural fit are assessed by the reporting manager. A formal check-in occurs at day 30, day 60, and day 90 with documented feedback.

Key Contacts: For payroll and benefits questions, contact hr@company.com. For laptop, VPN, or account issues, contact it-helpdesk@company.com. For expense or travel bookings, use the Finance Portal linked on the intranet homepage.

Remote Work Eligibility: Employees in eligible roles may request remote work arrangements up to 3 days per week, subject to manager approval. Remote work is not permitted for new hires during their probation period, for roles requiring on-site presence (e.g., facilities, security), or during critical business periods.

Home Office Setup: The company provides a one-time home office allowance of $500 for desk, chair, and internet equipment. Employees are responsible for maintaining a professional, ergonomic workspace. The company retains the right to conduct periodic home office compliance checks for health and safety.

Remote Work Expectations: Remote workers are expected to maintain core collaboration hours (10 AM - 3 PM in their local timezone), respond to messages within 2 hours, and attend all mandatory meetings in-person or via video conference. Employees must use company-issued laptops only; personal computers are not permitted.

Cybersecurity & Data Protection: All data accessed from home must be encrypted and stored only on company devices. Public Wi-Fi usage requires mandatory VPN connection. Printing of confidential documents at home is not permitted. Webcams must be covered when not in use.

Internet & Connectivity: The company does not provide internet subsidies. Employees are responsible for maintaining a minimum 20 Mbps download speed and 5 Mbps upload speed for video conferencing. Internet outages exceeding 2 hours should be reported to HR with supporting evidence (ISP outage confirmation).

Learning Budget: All employees receive an annual professional development budget of $2,000 (pro-rated for part-time employees) to spend on courses, certifications, conferences, and books. Unused budget does not roll over to the next year. Managers must approve all learning requests in advance.

Certification Support: The company reimburses 100% of exam fees for job-related certifications (e.g., AWS, Azure, PMP, CISSP) upon successful completion. Study materials and exam prep courses are covered under the learning budget. Employees are entitled to 2 days of paid study leave per certification exam.

Conference & Seminar Attendance: Employees may attend up to 2 external conferences per year with manager approval. The company covers registration fees, travel, and accommodation. Employees must share learnings via an internal presentation within 2 weeks of returning.

Internal Training & Mentorship: All new hires participate in a structured onboarding training program. Mentorship matching is facilitated by HR during the first month. Department-wide knowledge-sharing sessions are held monthly.

Tuition Reimbursement: Employees pursuing part-time university degrees or diplomas related to their role may receive tuition reimbursement up to $5,000 per year, conditional on maintaining a minimum GPA of 3.0 and remaining with the company for 12 months after course completion.

Data Classification: Personal data is classified into four tiers: Level 1 (Public), Level 2 (Internal), Level 3 (Confidential), and Level 4 (Restricted). Processing of Level 3 and 4 data requires explicit legal basis and documented Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with all third-party processors.

Lawful Basis for Processing: The company only processes personal data based on one of six lawful bases under GDPR: consent, contract performance, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests. All data processing activities must be documented in the Data Processing Register maintained by the Privacy Officer.

Data Subject Rights: Individuals have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict, port, and object to their personal data. Requests must be honored within 30 days of receipt. Erasure requests ('right to be forgotten') are granted unless legal retention obligations apply.

Data Breach Notification: Any suspected data breach involving personal data must be reported to the Privacy Officer within 24 hours. Breaches affecting >100 individuals or causing high risk must be reported to applicable data protection authorities within 72 hours and to affected individuals without undue delay.

International Data Transfers: Personal data transfers outside the EEA are prohibited unless Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or other GDPR-approved mechanisms are in place. Data transfers to the United States require review by the Privacy Officer due to regulatory uncertainty post-Schrems II.

Anti-Bribery & Corruption: The company prohibits all forms of bribery, kickbacks, or improper payments to government officials, business partners, or customers. This includes direct payments, gifts, meals, travel, or any other value transfers intended to obtain favorable business treatment.

Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) Compliance: All employees operating in or dealing with foreign governments must comply with the FCPA and similar anti-corruption laws in applicable jurisdictions. Violations carry severe criminal penalties including fines up to $2 million and imprisonment.

Sanctions & Export Controls: The company does not conduct business with individuals or entities on government sanctions lists (OFAC, EU, UN). Employees must conduct sanctions screening on all new customers, vendors, and partners. Export of controlled technologies (encryption, defense-related) requires regulatory licenses.

Anti-Money Laundering (AML): Employees must report suspicious financial activity that could indicate money laundering. Customer due diligence (CDD) and enhanced due diligence (EDD) are required for high-risk customers. The Compliance Officer reviews all transactions flagged by the automated AML screening system.

Whistleblower Protections: Employees who report suspected legal or compliance violations in good faith are protected from retaliation. Reports can be made anonymously through the third-party Ethics Hotline: 1-800-ETHICS-1. The Compliance Officer investigates all reports within 20 business days.
